instructions: Boil 1 cup of water. Put the dried porcini in a heatproof bowl, pour the hot water over them, and leave them for 10 to 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of water to a boil over high heat. Add 2 tsp of the salt.
Pull the stems off the shiitake and slice the caps. Chop them roughly.
Cook the fettuccine in the boiling water until it's 1 minute short of done. Scoop out 3/4 cup of the pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the shiitake and a pinch of salt. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until they're tender and lightly browned.
Lift the porcini out of their water and squeeze them dry. Chop them roughly, add them to the skillet and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the cream and scrape the bottom of the pan. Cook for about 2 minutes, until the cream has cooked down.
Add the mascarpone and 1/3 cup of the pasta water. Stir until the sauce is creamy.
Add the pasta and toss over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. If the sauce is too thick, add a splash of the remaining pasta water.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve right away in warm bowls.
method_notes: Skinny Spatula's Tagliatelle Funghi (4.94 from 65) is the lead, written here with fettuccine: browned shiitake and soaked porcini finished with cream and mascarpone in a loose sauce. Food.com's Fettuccine al Funghi (unrated) is a quicker cream and butter version with fresh mushrooms and nutmeg. I kept the lead's mushrooms and its cream and mascarpone, and the sauce is loosened with pasta water. There is no cheese or herb in the lead, so none was added.
